content: When you try to stay on the surface of the water, you sink; but when you try to sink, you float.
author: Alan Watts
sourceWork: The Book: On the Taboo Against Knowing Who You Are (1966)
story:
This insight touches directly on the messy reality of human nature. Living in pretense takes an enormous amount of mental energy. When you constantly manage impressions to please others, you end up feeling like an imposter in your own skin.

Across his life and work, Alan Watts saw how easily we surrender our tranquility to fear, vanity, and distraction. Honesty with yourself can feel uncomfortable at first, but it is the only ground upon which a real life can be built. When you stop lying to yourself about your feelings, your energy is immediately freed up.
reflectionPrompt: What current difficulty or obstacle are you facing that could become your greatest training ground?
